sections.heading: Build capability today. Take ownership when ready.
sections.body:
Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT) combines the setup and operation of a Global Capability Centre (GCC) with a planned handover to your organisation. Define the centre’s scope, operating responsibilities and transfer principles before delivery begins.

Unlike [strategy and setup advisory](/services/talent-advisory-gcc/gcc-strategy-setup), BOT includes a separately agreed build and operating phase. Unlike a [managed team](/services/talent-advisory-gcc/specialist-talent-managed-teams#managed-teams), it plans for centre ownership and a transfer decision. Linkfields is headquartered in South Africa with an offshore delivery centre in India.

sections.heading: What your centre is designed to retain
sections.description: The retained capability and handover scope are contractual decisions. Centre transfer does not imply ownership of all proprietary software.

items.title: Specialist capability and leadership
items.description: A capability and leadership model aligned to the centre’s agreed service scope.
items.bullets: Deliverable – team responsibilities, capability plan and knowledge-transfer requirements

items.title: Governed delivery and quality controls
items.description: Working practices and review gates that make scope, quality, risks and decisions visible.
items.bullets: Deliverable – governance model, acceptance criteria and delivery evidence

items.title: Tooling and operating knowledge
items.description: An agreed environment and tooling model with documented working practices.
items.bullets: Deliverable – environment inventory, operating documentation and rights register

sections.heading: A phased journey from setup to handover
sections.description: Build a GCC with a clear path to ownership. Phase responsibilities and acceptance evidence are agreed before the engagement; dates depend on scope and readiness.

items.title: Build
items.description: Agree the blueprint, then establish the team, environments and initial delivery practices within scope.
items.bullets:
Linkfields – build and launch the agreed capability
Client decision – approve scope, access and launch readiness
Exit evidence – responsibility map, onboarding plan and ready environments

items.title: Operate
items.description: Run agreed delivery, develop capability and review stabilisation and scaling needs.
items.bullets:
Linkfields – manage delivery and maintain operating evidence
Client decision – approve priorities, changes and scale
Exit evidence – delivery records, controls, documentation and readiness review

items.title: Transfer
items.description: Assess readiness and transition the agreed people, knowledge and operating responsibilities.
items.bullets:
Linkfields – prepare and execute the agreed handover
Client decision – accept scope, exceptions and future accountability
Exit evidence – signed acceptance record and continuity plan

sections.heading: Capability centres with embedded IP
sections.description: Build scalable delivery capacity with stronger governance and automation. Bring quality, security and engineering IP into your BOT centre where applicable. This supports capability development without promising a launch or transfer timeframe.

items.title: Delivery governance and quality IP
items.description: Configure agreed review practices, delivery evidence and testing or release-assurance packs around the centre’s work.
items.bullets:
Operate – name control and evidence owners
Retain – document the working model and agreed reusable artefacts

items.title: Cyber-Safe Delivery
items.description: Embed agreed security responsibilities and review gates into engineering and delivery workflows.
items.bullets:
Configure – access, code and release-control requirements
Operate – agree security review and escalation ownership
Retain – control documentation and agreed evidence

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: Consider composable enterprise applications where the centre’s work extends beyond ERP or CRM fit.
items.bullets:
Configure and operate – agree application scope and operator
Retain – agreed applications and documentation subject to contract
License – define continuing product-use rights separately

sections.heading: What transfers, what stays licensed
sections.description: This sample checklist shows what to agree, not proof of completed BOT engagements. Sustainable transfer depends on accepted capability, clear rights and documented operating knowledge.

items.title: People and operating responsibilities
items.description: Confirm named leadership, responsibilities and proposed people-transition arrangements, with knowledge-transfer requirements agreed before handover.
items.bullets:
Evidence – responsibility map and knowledge-transfer record
Gate – client accepts future accountability and unresolved people dependencies

items.title: Processes, environments and records
items.description: Check documented processes, environment inventories, access control, delivery records and operating instructions.
items.bullets:
Evidence – reviewed documentation and access-transition plan
Gate – agreed owners can operate the transferred scope

items.title: Software, IP and licences
items.description: Identify custom deliverables, reusable IP, proprietary products and third-party licences separately.
items.bullets:
Evidence – rights and licence register with restrictions
Gate – agreed ownership and continuing use rights
Boundary – Linkfields products remain separately licensed unless otherwise contracted

items.title: Acceptance and continuity
items.description: Agree the readiness criteria, exceptions, handover sequence and any continuity-support scope.
items.bullets:
Evidence – acceptance record and exception register
Gate – client approval of readiness and residual risks
Boundary – legal, entity and facility transfer must be explicitly agreed

sections.heading: Before we agree your ownership path

items.title: What does “hand it over” include?
items.description: The contract defines what transfers: people arrangements, operating responsibilities, environments, documentation and deliverables as applicable. Entity, legal and facility transfers must be explicitly scoped; they are not assumed.

items.title: Do we own all software and embedded IP afterwards?
items.description: No blanket ownership transfer is implied. Agree rights for custom deliverables, reusable accelerators, Linkfields products and third-party software separately. Proprietary products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without services.

items.title: How is readiness accepted?
items.description: Agree phase gates, required evidence, acceptance owners and exceptions before delivery. The client reviews operating capability, documentation, controls and rights, then accepts the agreed transfer scope and any residual risks.

items.title: What determines locations, timing and continuity?
items.description: Location, access approvals, team readiness, scope and contractual dependencies shape the plan. Agree working-hour coverage and any post-transfer support separately. There is no standard transfer date implied by this page.

items.title: How do BOT and commercial models relate?
items.description: BOT describes the build, operate and ownership-transition model. Fixed Price, Time & Materials, Managed Service, Dedicated Team and Outcome-Based are [commercial models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models). Select them against phase scope and evidence; Outcome-Based fees require agreed measurable outcomes.

items.title: What should we bring to the first discussion?
items.description: Share the capability scope, current centre stage, location constraints and intended transfer objective. We can agree an NDA before detailed discovery, then define the assessment and ownership questions together.
